about.title: Personal Injury Help in Fairfax, California
about.longDescription: Fairfax is a small, tight-knit Marin County town, but its streets still see their share of collisions. Public records show 17 injury collisions in the most recent final crash year, leaving 19 people hurt and, tragically, 1 traffic death. Sir Francis Drake Boulevard, Bolinas Road, Broadway, and Center Boulevard carry the most reported crash activity in town, and Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. see the most reports. If you were hurt anywhere in Fairfax, sorting out medical bills, missed work, and insurance calls can feel overwhelming on top of recovering physically. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney in the area — we are not a law firm, and we don't handle your case ourselves. The attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. Reaching out costs you nothing and there's no obligation to move forward. If you or someone you love was injured in a crash near Sir Francis Drake Boulevard, Bolinas Road, or anywhere else in Fairfax, it may help to talk with someone who understands California injury law before dealing with insurance adjusters alone.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Settling

items.title: You Have Two Years — But It Passes Fast
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim, though claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting to see how you feel could cost you the chance to recover anything at all.

items.title: Partial Fault Won't Erase Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you're found partly responsible for a crash, you can still recover damages — just reduced by your share of fault. An attorney can help make sure your portion of blame isn't overstated by an insurer.

items.title: No Cap on What You Can Recover for Pain and Suffering
items.desc: Unlike some states, California places no cap on non-economic damages — like pain, suffering, and emotional distress — in ordinary injury cases. That matters when an injury changes your daily life beyond just medical bills.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover Something
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so you don't pay out of pocket to get advice or representation. They only get paid if you receive a settlement or award.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Fairfax?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a lawsuit. If your injury involved a government entity, such as a public road crew or transit vehicle, the deadline to file a notice can be as short as six months. It's wise to talk with an attorney well before either deadline approaches.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the crash?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, so being partly responsible doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault. An attorney can help make sure the fault assigned to you is fair and accurate.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Fairfax?
items.answer: Public crash records show that Sir Francis Drake Boulevard, Bolinas Road, Broadway, and Center Boulevard have the highest reported collision counts in Fairfax, with Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. showing the most reports. These are neutral public-record counts, not a judgment about any road's safety.

items.question: Will I owe money upfront to speak with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive's connection service is free, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you receive a settlement or award. There's no upfront cost or obligation to move forward after speaking with someone.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney. We don't provide legal representation ourselves, and any advice or case handling would come from the attorney you're connected with.
